citation.title: Climate obstruction in the Global South: Future research trajectories

question: Where and in what form does climate obstruction appear in the Global South, given that most research has focused on the Global North, especially the United States; the paper sets out a future research agenda.
data: No original data. A short opinion paper (5 pages) drawing on 14 cited references and a few country examples (Vietnam, India, Latin America). No period, sample or size.
method: No classification or counting method. Argument and agenda-setting; Table 1 lists research topics and questions.

definitions.definition: Campaigns and other policy actions by well-organised and financed networks of corporate and other actors who have sought to prevent global and/or national action on climate change over four decades.
definitions.quote: campaigns and other policy actions led by well-organized and financed networks of corporate and other actors

definitions.definition: Efforts include organised mainstream and social media campaigns, lobbying, funding politicians and campaigns, and spreading climate-delaying discourses and practices.
definitions.quote: organized mainstream and social media campaigns, lobbying, funding politicians and political campaigns, and disseminating climatedelaying discourses and practices

findings.claim: Most research on climate obstruction has focused on the Global North, especially the US.
findings.quote: most of the research on climate obstruction has focused on countries in the Global North, especially the United States.

findings.claim: In the Global South climate delay is a frequent obstruction tactic, often tied to economic growth or energy poverty justifications.
findings.quote: climate delay is a frequently deployed tactic of climate obstruction and is often linked to a justification for expanded economic growth

findings.claim: Example: in Vietnam, ties between state-owned Vinacomin, Electricity of Vietnam and a ministry slowed renewable energy progress (cited to a news article, ref 4).
findings.quote: these three entities to slow progress

findings.claim: Sector differs by region: fossil fuel industry leads obstruction in the US, while agribusiness is more prominent in Latin America (cited to ref 9).
findings.quote: the agribusiness sector, one of the fastest-growing contributors to emissions

findings.claim: There is growing evidence of ties between US, Japanese and European financial and private sector institutions and high-carbon sectors in the Global South (cited to ref 10).
findings.quote: ties between, for example, USA, Japanese, and

findings.claim: Civil society in many Global South countries is constrained by limited space and financing, and sometimes repressed (Vietnam anti-coal activists prosecuted).
findings.quote: the constricted space for civil society groups in many global South countries and lack of

findings.claim: Obstruction actors, including non-state actors, corporations and think tanks, appear to have increased influence after COP26 and COP27, in the context of the Ukraine invasion and gas and coal re-emerging.
findings.quote: appear to have increased their influence on climate discourse

recommendations.claim: Future research should examine whether and in what form climate obstruction appears in the Global South.
recommendations.quote: a future research agenda needs to shine greater light on if and in what form climate obstruction in the Global South appears.

recommendations.claim: Research is needed on how domestic actors, including the state and corporations, respond to, and are funded by, transnational networks.

recommendations.claim: Common but differentiated responsibility should shape how obstruction is understood in the Global South.

Priority research directions include developmentalism discourses, negotiating blocs at the negotiations, political leaders and coalitions, transnational links, sovereignty claims, climate nationalism, and domestic energy industries (Table 1).
recommendations.quote: negotiating blocs at the negotiations, political leaders and their coalitions, transnational links,

limitations.point: Authors state the list of research directions is not exhaustive.
Authors state that theory on climate obstruction is rooted in US experience, and Global South theory is still developing.
limitations.quote: conceptual and theoretical understandings of climate obstruction in the Global South are under development.

limitations.point: Authors note the Global South is not homogeneous, so generalisation is limited.
limitations.quote: The Global South is not a homogenous group

limitations.point: Opinion paper with no original data, no sampling or classification method, and no definition of business or fossil-fuel linkage that could be operationalised. Peer-review status of this article type is not stated in the text. Its own examples rest on news articles and secondary sources. It does not address COP delegations or badges.

The PDF text extraction (pypdf) shows hyphenation artefacts at line breaks, so some quotes contain a hyphen where the original line broke (for example 'orga-nized'). The PDF could not be rendered as images (no pdftoppm), so the text layer was read. No instructions to a reader or AI were found in the source.
